sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Stone County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Every Stone County deed ends up with the Recorder of Deeds on East Fourth Street in Galena, suite 108-A. The phone is 417-357-6362, and the counter keeps weekday hours of eight to four. Amy Larson is the elected Recorder, and the Recorder's page lists a team of deputy recorders.

The same desk handles federal and state liens, DD-214 discharge papers and marriage licenses, and license applications need an appointment.

Paper records held in the Galena office reach back to 1851, the year Stone County was organized. For anything newer, the iCounty portal at stonemo.icounty.com carries records from January 1, 1993 to today.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Stone County?
sections.html:
Phone the office for the exact total on your deed before it goes in the mail. Missouri law builds the price from a statutory base plus state user fees, and the final number depends on page count and the document type.

The fee picture shifted this year. The Stone County Recorder posted a release saying a flat $2.00 increase under Senate Bill 938 applied statewide from August 28, 2026, to recorded documents, marriage licenses and surveys or plats. Any price sheet printed before that day is $2 short.

Recorder charges named in RSMo 59.310 for Stone County filings
ServiceStatutory amount
Recording a deed, first page$5
Recording, each added page$3
Copy of a recorded instrumentCapped at $2, then $1 a page
Certificate and seal$1
Release covering several items$5 for every extra item
Subdivision plat, per sheet$25
Surcharge for a nonconforming document$25

None of these figures include the state user fees collected under RSMo 59.319, which were also rewritten by the 2026 bill.

sections.h2: How should a deed be prepared before it goes to Galena?
sections.html:
Reserve a three inch band at the head of page one for the Recorder's stamp, with three-quarters of an inch of clear paper along the other edges. A deed that fails this test can come back with a written reason, or the office can take it for the $25 surcharge.

  • Use unbound sheets, white or light, printed on a single side in dark ink.
  • Set type at eight points or larger, with each signer's name typed below the signature.
  • Show the title, date, grantors and their marital status, grantees and legal description on page one under that band.
  • List one grantee's mailing address.

Without a legal description or a grantee address the Recorder may not file the deed. The statute says the deed's validity and constructive notice survive that omission, yet the office will still decline it.

sections.h2: How does the Recorder connect to Stone County property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor maps parcel lines from warranty deeds supplied by the Recorder, so an unrecorded deed leaves the map behind. Matt Daugherty is the Assessor, at 106 East Fifth Street in Galena, with real estate staff at 417-357-6145. His office typically closes the assessment books around July 1, and taxing districts generally set rates by September 1.

Anna Burk is the Collector, working from the Historic Courthouse at 108 East Fourth Street, phone 417-357-6124. Her office announced that 2026 statements would be mailed on Friday, November 13, 2026, and that online payment would open on November 6. Payment is due by December 31, with delinquency starting January 1, and a mailed check must be postmarked by December 31. Cards cost 2.4 percent with a $1.95 floor. The courthouse has a drop box at its north entrance, emptied daily.

The Collector no longer takes card numbers spoken over the phone, so pay at the counter or call the payment line printed on the statement.

  • Recorder of Deeds: 417-357-6362.
  • Assessor, real estate: 417-357-6145.
  • Assessor, personal property: 417-357-6141.
  • Collector of Revenue: 417-357-6124.

sections.h2: Is a senior tax freeze available in Stone County?
sections.html:
A senior property tax credit freeze exists in Missouri, and Stone County runs it through the Collector's office, where Jackie Daugherty is named as the SB190 Tax Freeze Lead. The Collector's home page currently says the application process is closed for this cycle.

An owner who qualifies can phone 417-357-6124 to learn when applications reopen and what paperwork to bring. Webster County describes the same credit as a limit on residential real estate tax growth for a primary residence. It leaves the bill in place and skips vehicle tax.

Before signing a sale contract, ask the Collector what a mid-year sale does to an approved freeze.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Stone County homes?
sections.html:
Stone County reached an estimated 32,503 residents by July 1, 2025, according to the Census Bureau, which is 4.6 percent above its 2020 base. Warren County grew 9.8 percent and Webster County 10.1 percent over the same stretch, so Stone is the slowest of the three.

Owners occupy 83.3 percent of homes here. Owned homes carried a median value of $249,000 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and rent was $896. One resident in three is 65 or older (33.3 percent), well above Warren County's 20.5 percent.

The county lists 21,225 housing units but just 13,530 households. The gap is homes that are not a household's usual address, which is useful context for anyone selling one.

sections.h2: What is Stone County like for a seller?
sections.html:
The county covers 511 square miles in southwest Missouri, and 47 of them are water. It borders Christian, Taney and Barry counties in Missouri, plus Lawrence County and Carroll County, Arkansas. The cities are Branson West, Crane, Galena, Hurley, Reeds Spring and Kimberling City, the largest. Branson sits mostly in Taney County, and Stone County was part of the Branson micropolitan area until 2023.

Census data hints at a visitor economy. Accommodation and food services sales were $109.9 million in 2022, against $44.3 million in Warren County and $44.1 million in Webster County. Just 49.5 percent of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

Schools are run by Blue Eye R-V, Crane R-III, Galena R-II, Hurley R-I and Reeds Spring R-IV, and Shell Knob 78 operates a single elementary. Check the district named on the tax statement.

The county's population stood at 9,921 in 1970, then rose to 15,587 in 1980, 28,658 in 2000 and 32,202 in 2010, before the 2020 census counted 31,076. Part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county, and the county was named for William Stone, an early Maryland settler who later served as Taney County judge.

sections.h2: How can an owner avoid overpaying for a copy of a deed?
sections.html:
Go to the Recorder directly. The office has warned residents about mailers from outside companies that offer a certified deed copy for $87 or more, then simply order it from the county. State law caps a Recorder's copy at $2 for page one and $1 for each added page, with $1 more for a certificate.

The Recorder's page also points to DeedWatch.com, a free email alert that fires when a document is recorded against the names or addresses you list. The service cannot stop fraud, and the Recorder calls it an early warning.

faqs.q: Where is the Stone County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 108-A East Fourth Street, Galena, MO 65656. The phone is 417-357-6362, and the office is staffed weekdays from eight to four.

faqs.q: Can I search Stone County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, from January 1, 1993 forward through the county's iCounty portal. Older records sit in the Galena office, which holds paper back to 1851.

faqs.q: Did Missouri recording fees go up in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Senate Bill 938 added a flat $2.00 starting August 28, 2026, on recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats or surveys. Ask for the total on your page count.

faqs.q: What if my deed misses the margin rules?
faqs.a: The Recorder may return it with a reason or record it for an extra $25. Page one needs a three inch blank band at the top.

faqs.q: When are Stone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By December 31, with delinquency from January 1. The 2026 statements were mailed November 13, 2026, and the Collector's line is 417-357-6124.
